deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and is not in Riemann's hand. It is a historical note, headed 'Seite 9.' and numbered '(1'. It was evidently written by the editor of Riemann's posthumous paper 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', Karl Hattendorff, who edited it from Riemann's papers; it appeared in Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867. The first person ('als mir ... zu Händen kamen', 'als er es mir aushändigte') fits the editor.

Content, step by step:
(i) Riemann's paper on the surface of least area with given boundary was already printed when the writer received the Berlin Academy's Monatsberichte for October and December 1866.
(ii) These contain Weierstrass's paper 'Über die Flächen, deren mittlere Krümmung überall gleich Null ist'.
(iii) As with Abelian functions, the two great mathematicians met on the minimal-surface (Plateau) problem, and their investigations fall at nearly the same time.
(iv) It quotes Weierstrass (Monatsberichte 1866, p. 612): he presents his main results to the Academy, noting that he had lectured on part of them several years earlier in the mathematical seminar of the University (Berlin).
(v) It records Riemann's own statement that his manuscript was five to six years old in April 1866, when he handed it to the writer. That dates Riemann's work to about 1860–61.

The purpose is a priority remark comparing the independent, near-contemporaneous treatments of minimal surfaces by Riemann and Weierstrass. Riemann treats the Plateau problem for polygonal and other boundaries via conformal mapping and the Gauss map. Weierstrass treats the Weierstrass(–Enneper) representation and minimal surfaces through given curves. The previous page is a draft of the same passage.
errors: The historical statements are consistent with the record: Weierstrass's note is in Monatsberichte der Königl. Preuss. Akad. d. Wiss. zu Berlin 1866, beginning p. 612; Riemann's paper appeared in 1867 with an editorial remark of this kind.
Minor: the writer says the October and December Monatsberichte; Weierstrass's communication was presented in 1866 and the cited page 612 lies in that volume, so no evident slip.

results.what: Priority and dating note: Riemann's minimal-surface manuscript dated by Riemann himself to ca. 1860–61; Weierstrass's 1866 Berlin note and his earlier seminar lectures cited for comparison.
results.modern_name: History of the Plateau problem / Weierstrass–Enneper representation; Riemann's posthumous 'Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt'
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous, ed. Hattendorff 1867) and Weierstrass (1866) independently; Enneper (1864) for the representation formulas

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial historical note, almost certainly by Hattendorff, that corresponds to the remark printed with Riemann's posthumous minimal-surface paper (1867). The dating of Riemann's work to about 1860–61 and the parallel with Weierstrass are already part of the published record. The page contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out words after 'es ist' are heavily cancelled and essentially illegible; '[-wegen[?] allein[?]-]' is speculative and could be dropped or marked as illegible.
'Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' and 'über die Flächen, deren mittlere Krümmung überall gleich Null ist' are underlined in the original.
'Weierstraß' is written in Latin script with ß/ss ('Weierstrass'), distinct from the surrounding Kurrent.
A pencil archival foliation '56' is visible at the right margin; '(1' at top right is the writer's own page number.
